answer_text: A stack is a linear data structure where insertion and removal both happen at the same end, called the top. Debugging tools can help illustrate how this kind of process actually behaves at runtime. This gives it Last In First Out behavior — the last item pushed onto the stack is the first one popped off. This topic is frequently covered in technical interviews as well as coursework. A queue, in contrast, inserts elements at the rear and removes them from the front, giving it First In First Out behavior, so the earliest inserted element is the first one to be removed.
